flags: BLM places the route in the National Scenic Byways Program, but the cache does not establish a formal National Scenic Byway designation or the catalog’s 2000 BLM designation date. Those specific designation claims are omitted.
Material strip miles run north-to-south; this narrative follows BLM’s south-to-north itinerary in reverse strip order: Terry, Brockway, Circle, Vida, then the Missouri crossing.

Wikipedia’s Circle page places a Great Northern station in 1914; the Gladstone Hotel page says the railroad was not completed through Circle until 1929. Railway arrival dates are omitted. The museum depot is explicitly identified as Northern Pacific, not conflated with Great Northern.
The historic bridge once carried Highway 13. The cache supports viewing it but establishes no pedestrian access, present vehicular use or replacement-bridge details.
The cache gives little detail on the road’s original builders or the Regina–Yellowstone Trail’s promotion. No construction motive or designation campaign is invented.
